sources.entry: OmniMac - Dynamic Island for any Mac (notch or not) plus ten more utilities in one lightweight menu-bar app: keep-awake, ⌘Tab by windows, window shortcuts and layouts, clipboard history, per-app volume and equaliser, performance monitor, OCR and app cleaner.

summary.one_liner: OmniMac is a free, open-source macOS menu-bar app that adds a Dynamic Island-style notch overlay (which also works on Macs without a notch) plus ten other utilities such as keep-awake, ⌘Tab by windows, window snapping, clipboard history, per-app volume and equaliser, performance monitoring, OCR and an app cleaner.
summary.what_it_does: The notch overlay expands on hover to show music, a file tray with AirDrop, today's calendar, sound controls, a timer/Pomodoro, and performance stats, and it can show alerts for track changes, AirPods connection, and charger wattage. Keep awake can stay on indefinitely, on a timer, or until a set time, including closed-lid mode via a sudoers rule that the user must install. ⌘Tab switches between individual windows with live thumbnails, and window shortcuts provide halves, thirds, quarters, snapping, and saved layouts on ⌃⌥1…9. The clipboard module keeps text, image and file history with pins and skips password manager content, and the sound module offers per-app volume and a 10-band equaliser. The performance module shows per-core CPU, GPU, memory, disk, network, temperature, battery health, and per-app resource use, while tools cover screenshots, scrolling capture, OCR, a colour picker, and an app cleaner that moves leftovers to the Trash. A Downloads module can offer to install .dmg apps when enabled, and every module can be switched off.
use_cases: replace Amphetamine for keeping a Mac awake
snap and arrange windows with keyboard shortcuts
keep a clipboard history with pins
adjust per-app volume and equalise audio on a Mac
monitor CPU, memory, temperature and battery health
uninstall apps and remove leftover files
how_to_run: Or download OmniMac.pkg and open it
notable: Dynamic Island-style notch overlay that also works on Macs without a notch, sized to the display
Bundles about eleven utilities in one menu-bar app, measured at roughly 0.017–0.033% CPU and 86 MB at idle
Clipboard history skips content copied from password managers and can paste without formatting
Published, reproducible idle-resource measurement method with scripts in the repo
Every module can be turned off and then frees its resources
caveats: Not notarized with a paid Apple developer account, so macOS blocks first launch until the user clicks Open Anyway in Privacy & Security
Closed-lid mode requires installing a sudoers rule that lets any program running as the user change the sleep setting without a password while it exists
Requires macOS 14.2 (Sonoma) or later; only tested on Apple silicon per the README
Notch reads now-playing info only from Spotify and Music
